Translate PTM tokens into readable modification names

Source: R/ptm.R
translate_ptm.Rd

The PTM column of pep_all is search-engine-specific:

Usage

translate_ptm(x, tol = 0.01, reference = ptm_reference())

Arguments

x

Character vector of PTM tokens. The payload is taken from inside () or [] when present, else the whole string. NA and "" pass through.

tol

Delta-mass matching tolerance in Da. The default 0.01 is wide enough for 2-decimal rounding ([+15.99]) and still separates near-neighbours such as Acetyl (42.010565) from Trimethyl (42.046950).

reference

Lookup table; defaults to ptm_reference(). The first row within tol wins, so row order encodes the preference between mass-degenerate modifications.

Value

A character vector the same length as x, with recognised tokens replaced by their modification name.

Details

  • DIA-NN writes UniMod accessions — (UniMod:35)

  • FragPipe writes monoisotopic delta masses behind a position+residue prefix — 2M(15.9949)

  • PEAKS writes the modification name — Oxidation (M) — and carries the delta mass in the peptide string instead; bracketed delta masses ([+15.99]) still turn up in some exports

This maps all of those onto one readable name, so PTM plots are comparable across engines. Handling the delta-mass form matters because it is what the project's default (FragPipe) data uses, and a token that is already a name simply passes through unchanged.

Display-time only — pep_all$PTM itself is left raw, following the same "data keys unchanged" rule as the report's renamed display labels.

Translation is name-only: the residue and position prefix (2M in 2M(15.9949)) is dropped, because the engines disagree on how they are written, so equivalent modifications collapse onto a single plot row. A token that matches nothing is returned unchanged rather than becoming NA.

See also

ptm_reference() for the table, plot_ptm_heatmap() which applies this at plot time.

Examples

translate_ptm(c("(UniMod:35)", "2M(15.9949)", "[+15.99]", "N-term(42.0106)"))
#> [1] "Oxidation" "Oxidation" "Oxidation" "Acetyl"   
translate_ptm("(UniMod:9999)")   # unknown accession, returned unchanged
#> [1] "(UniMod:9999)"
